judged_text: findMembers attaches no rejection handler to the Discourse.ajax promise, and both callers (routes' setupController and the pager actions) invoke it fire-and-forget without returning/propagating it, so any server failure is swallowed. When /groups/:name/members.json returns an error, the user sees an empty member list (or the previous page's stale list after next/previous) with no error message; the rejected promise is unhandled and the failure is invisible.

When /groups/:name/members.json returns an error, the user sees an empty member list (or the previous page's stale list after next/previous) with no error message; the rejected promise is unhandled and the failure is invisible.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Group#findMembers` returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise but has no `.catch`/rejection handling. More importantly, both `AdminGroupRoute.setupController` and `group-members` route `setupController` now call `model.findMembers();` without returning/chaining the promise (they removed the previous `afterModel` that returned the promise). That means an AJAX failure to `/groups/:name/members.json` will not trigger Ember’s route error/loading handling and will leave `model.members` unset/stale (templates render `{{each member in members}}` / `{{#each m in members}}`), resulting in an empty/stale list with no surfaced error. The finding is slightly overstated about the pager actions being fire-and-forget (they do `return group.findMembers();`), but the silent failure behavior on initial load is verifiable from the diff.
